title: Landscape composition shapes biological control by promoting off‐season predator diversity
content:
Our work demonstrates how off-season crop management and landscape structure jointly support overwintering predator populations and sustain their biological control potential. Specifically, by enhancing winter ground cover and preserving small fields, local rice growers can enjoy cost-free pest biological control and avoid crop protection expenditures in the next cropping cycle.


Abstract

Landscape heterogeneity can enhance biodiversity, but its impacts are rarely disaggregated over time. Thus, off-season effects on ecosystem service providers, service delivery and underlying (ecological) determinants often remain occluded. We assessed how landscape structure affects predator biodiversity in subtropical rice systems during winter. Furthermore, we investigated the impact of resident predator populations on the adult abundance of the overwintering generation rice stem borer Chilo suppressalis. To study these dynamics, 32,396 insect predators belonging to 52 species (19 families) were systematically surveyed in 19 fallow rice fields over a span of 3 years. Landscape composition and configuration jointly defined overwintering predator diversity, with the former exhibiting the strongest impacts. Rice fields with winter crop cover embedded in complex landscapes harboured the most diverse predator populations. Field size and forest proximity increased abundance and richness of specific natural enemy taxa, that is carabid beetles and hunting spiders. This, in turn, shaped biological control: across sites and years, overwintering pest abundance was negatively correlated with predator richness. Synthesis and applications. Our work demonstrates how off-season crop management and landscape structure jointly support overwintering predator populations and sustain their biological control potential. Specifically, by enhancing winter ground cover and preserving small fields, local rice growers can enjoy cost-free pest biological control and avoid crop protection expenditures in the next cropping cycle.

中文摘要

景观异质性可提升生物多样性，但其时间维度的影响机制却极少被分解研究。生态系统服务供给者、服务传递和潜在的(生态)决定因素的非生长季效应仍常被忽视。 本研究评估了亚热带水稻生态系统中景观结构如何影响越冬期捕食性天敌多样性，进一步分析了常见捕食性天敌种群对翌年越冬代二化螟种群成虫数量的调控作用。通过连续三年对19个梯度景观样点休耕稻田的系统调查，共采集32,396头捕食性天敌，分属19科52种。 景观组成和景观配置共同决定了冬季稻田捕食天敌的多样性，但景观组成的调控效应显著更强。嵌入复杂景观且具有冬季作物种植的稻田，支持捕食性天敌的多样性最高。田块大小与邻近森林的程度增加步甲和游猎型蜘蛛等天敌类群的丰度和丰富度。进而塑造了生物控害功能:跨年度与跨田块分析表明，越冬害虫种群数量与捕食性天敌丰富度呈负相关。 综合与应用:本研究诠释了非生长季作物管理与景观结构如何协同支持越冬捕食性天敌种群并维持其生物控害潜力。具体而言，通过增加冬季作物种植的同时，适当保留小规模农田生境，有助于提升天敌生物防治的支持功能，并有效减少翌年下一茬作物害虫防控的投入。
